prompt:
Create one companion TripLOG expense-linking mockup board with two related 390 × 844 mobile screens side by side, total 820 × 844 CSS pixels. Match the attached user-provided reference's established TripLOG design tone and component styling. The real client date is October 31, 2026; all booking/payment dates below are fictional example data. Left screen: “예약 편집”, retaining a compact reservation form for “시부야 스카이”, use date “10.28 수 18:30”, reference “A1B2C3D4”, and an original-ticket link. Integrate a small lower section “금액 · 지출 연동”, not a financial dashboard: amount field “JPY ¥2,700”, enabled “지출 자동 연동”, and concise choices “새 지출 기록 / 기존 지출 연결”. Collapse secondary payment options into one short row “10.15 · 카드 · 나” with a chevron. A quiet expense preview reads “관광 · 사전구매 · 25,650원”; show “예시 환율 100엔 = 950원” as small secondary text. Yellow footer action “저장”. Right screen: “기존 지출 연결”, a small reservation-context strip, search, and a concise selectable expense list. Select the matching “시부야 스카이 / 25,650원 / JPY ¥2,700 / 2026.10.15 · 카드 · 나 / 관광 · 사전구매”; show one unrelated expense row unselected. Use a compact linked-record summary and yellow “이 지출과 연결” footer action. The chosen existing expense is reused, without creating a duplicate. Keep short Korean labels, readable compact fields, small category icons, edit/copy/chevron conventions and restrained spacing consistent with the reference. Payment remains a secondary section inside reservation editing. Do not add reservation-total/remaining-balance panels, charts, payment histories, extra explanatory paragraphs, uploads, hotel hero cards or a redesigned main wallet.

Input images:
- reference.png: the user's selected TripLOG mockup, used as the design-tone reference for this related expense-linking flow.

inputs.role: User-provided selected TripLOG mockup as design-tone reference

notes: Expense linkage stays inside reservation editing, not the wallet overview.
Reuse an explicitly selected existing expense instead of generating a duplicate.
Booking/payment dates, prices and exchange rate are illustrative.
